latest.name: OpenRouter — Multi-model AI API Gateway
latest.short_verdict: A developer-focused gateway that exposes hundreds of third-party AI models through one OpenAI-compatible API and a browser chat. Its free tier lists 25+ free models and 4 providers, with free-model requests capped at 20 per minute and 50 per day. The main trade-off is that free-model availability and quality vary by upstream provider; it is best for prototyping and model evaluation, not production reliability.
latest.what_it_does: OpenRouter provides one account, model catalogue and API endpoint for calling models from many providers. Developers can compare and switch models without rewriting their integration, use an OpenAI-compatible chat-completions API, browse model pricing and provider availability, and use the browser chat for manual experiments. It is an AI infrastructure/API gateway, not an IDE code-completion assistant.
latest.why_try_it: Useful for developers prototyping an AI feature, comparing free models, or adding model choice to an app without integrating each provider separately. The browser chat offers a no-code way to try available free models; API use requires creating an account and API key. Its use case is distinct from code completion (GitHub Copilot) and pull-request review (CodeRabbit) already in the history.
latest.free_tier: Official pricing page lists 25+ free models, 4 free providers, browser chat and API access, activity logs, up to 5 workspaces, and no platform fee. Free model variants (model IDs ending in :free) have a $0 model price and are capped at 20 requests/minute and 50 requests/day for accounts that have purchased less than $10 in credits. Free model availability changes over time. API requests require an account/API key; browser chat is available through the website.
latest.limits: Free plan excludes paid models and advanced controls such as budgets/spend controls, preferred-provider routing, prompt caching, management API keys, data-policy routing, SSO and private endpoints. Free model endpoints can be rate-limited or unavailable by upstream providers; failed requests may count toward the daily cap. Buying at least $10 in credits raises the free-model daily cap to 1,000 requests but is a paid top-up and is not required for the basic free tier. Provider/model terms, context limits, latency and data handling differ; review each model's terms before use. Do not send confidential client or personal data unless the selected model/provider data terms are acceptable.
latest.signup_pakistan: OpenRouter's Terms of Service checked on 2026-11-20 require users to be at least 18 and do not explicitly name Pakistan as excluded. They warn that individual model providers may impose country/region restrictions, so availability can vary by model. Pakistan signup was not independently tested. The free tier lists no payment method requirement; paid credit checkout acceptance for Pakistani cards or local payment methods was not verified. Free-model availability in the browser/API should therefore be treated as subject to provider restrictions.
latest.quality_evidence: Vendor-reported adoption: OpenRouter's homepage displayed 800T+ monthly tokens, 10M+ users, 600+ models and 80+ providers on 2026-11-20; these are company claims, not independently audited. Vendor usage signal: its free-model rankings are based on token volume processed through OpenRouter over the trailing seven days, which measures platform usage rather than model quality. Independent research: a 2026 NYU Stern thesis analyses weekly OpenRouter model-market data from 2025-08-24 to 2026-02-22, evidence that the marketplace is used as a research dataset, not a product quality benchmark. Anecdotal community feedback is mixed: Reddit users report useful experimentation but also intermittent provider rate limits, latency and inconsistent free endpoints. No standardized independent benchmark of OpenRouter itself was verified.
latest.android_status: No official first-party OpenRouter Android app was verified in Google Play research. Third-party Android clients that connect to OpenRouter exist, but they are independent apps and are not endorsed or published by OpenRouter. Use the browser chat or API instead.
